name: Tablet computers
title: Why GO Corporation failed, and when tablets became viable
question: Why did GO Corporation's pen computers fail, and when did tablets become viable?
answer: GO Corporation (1987) built PenPoint, an operating system for pen tablets, and was sold to AT&T in 1994 before being shut down. Pen recognition, weight and battery life were not good enough for a general computer. The iPad (2010) used capacitive multitouch, an ARM chip and a lithium-ion battery: the stack the iPhone had just proved.
verdict_reason: The iPhone's multitouch and ARM stack (2007) made the iPad (2010) possible.

constraint.name: Touch input and battery life
constraint.detail: Pen recognition of the early 1990s was error-prone, and the hardware was heavy with short battery life.

crossing.text: Capacitive multitouch and ARM SoCs proven in phones.
